summary_oneline: Providers are already lazy-imported; the real ~192ms startup cost is navconfig+datamodel+jinja2 pulled in by notify/providers/base.py

localization.role: package entrypoint; imports providers.base, Notify, install_uvloop — no concrete provider
already-lazy provider resolution via importlib; also the bad missing-dependency diagnostic
eagerly imports .conf (navconfig) and .templates (jinja2) for symbols used only inside __getattr__
existing PEP 562 precedent for deferral in this module
the single hot path: pulls navconfig, notify.models (datamodel) and notify.templates (jinja2)
annotation-only uses of Actor — removable via TYPE_CHECKING
sole call site of is_template_source, the reason jinja2 is on the import path
pure string predicate with no jinja2 dependency, trapped in a jinja2-importing module
evaluates navconfig at import time to build TEMPLATE_DIR and ~20 other constants
core deps carrying four provider-only/server-only packages (emoji, aiobotocore, pillow, cloudpickle)
in-tree precedent: deferred import with an actionable 'install the extra' message
server path also routes through the lazy factory — no second eager surface

constraints.statement: The Notify factory already lazy-imports providers via importlib and memoises in PROVIDERS; a 'lazy provider import' feature has no work left to do at that layer.
constraints.implication: The feature must be re-aimed at the base/conf/templates import chain, or it delivers nothing measurable.

constraints.statement: notify/providers/__init__.py is a bare docstring and there is no downward import of any concrete provider anywhere in the package.
constraints.implication: No eager fan-out exists to remove; the requester's premise does not hold as stated.

constraints.statement: Public surface is tiny: __all__ = ('Notify','ProviderType'); tests import providers by full module path, never via a package re-export.
constraints.implication: PEP 562 laziness at the package root is backward-compatible and cannot break the existing suite.
Any DeprecationWarning emitted by a lazy shim fails the whole suite; shims must be silent.

constraints.statement: Provider SDKs are already declared as optional extras; README documents none of them.
constraints.implication: The install story is half-built — the extras exist but are undiscoverable, which is why a missing SDK produces an unactionable error.

constraints.statement: Telegram.py:343-347 and notify/utils/uv.py:14 already model the 'deferred import + name the extra' pattern.
constraints.implication: Follow the existing idiom rather than inventing a new one.

constraints.statement: notify.exceptions and notify/types/typedefs are Cython modules requiring build_ext --inplace.
constraints.implication: Any worktree used for this feature needs a Cython rebuild before tests; import-time measurements must be taken against built extensions.

recent_history.message: feat(templateparser-refactor): TASK-010 — lazy TemplateEnv singleton via PEP 562
recent_history.relevance: establishes the deferral idiom this feature extends

recent_history.message: fix: make uvloop optional and build Windows wheels
feat(jinja-string-notify): TASK-015 — three-way template= dispatch in ProviderBase._prepare_
recent_history.relevance: introduced the is_template_source call that put jinja2 on the startup path

whats_new: A jinja2-free home for is_template_source (e.g. notify/templates/_predicates.py or notify/utils/), re-exported from notify.templates for compatibility.
An extras-aware error path in LoadProvider that distinguishes 'unknown provider' from 'provider's optional dependency missing' and names the extra to install.
A PROVIDER_EXTRAS mapping (provider name -> extra name) to drive that message.
A startup-cost regression test asserting that `import notify` leaves jinja2/datamodel (and ideally navconfig) out of sys.modules.
README section documenting which extra installs which provider.

whats_changed.change: move Actor behind TYPE_CHECKING (annotation-only, F006) and is_template_source to a jinja2-free module or a function-local import
defer `from .conf import TEMPLATE_DIR` and `from .templates import TemplateParser` into __getattr__, their only consumer
fix the dead __import__ fallback that returns a module instead of the class, and emit an extras-aware ImportError message
demote emoji, aiobotocore, pillow (unused) and cloudpickle (server-only) out of core into the appropriate extras

non_goals: Making notify/providers/* lazy — already lazy (F002, F004).
Building a provider registry, plugin discovery, or entry-points system.
Changing the ProviderBase / _send_ contract or any provider's runtime behaviour.
Reducing install size of the `all` extra.

integration_risks.risk: Deferring navconfig is the only way to reach the big win (~122ms of 192ms), but notify/conf.py exports ~20 module-level constants consumed across the server and providers; making it lazy is a far larger change than the base.py deferrals.
integration_risks.mitigation: Stage it: land the datamodel+jinja2 deferrals first (bounded, ~69ms), then evaluate a PEP 562 conf module separately with its own measurement.

integration_risks.risk: TYPE_CHECKING on Actor changes runtime annotation resolution; anything calling typing.get_type_hints() on ProviderBase methods would break.
integration_risks.mitigation: Add `from __future__ import annotations` and grep for get_type_hints before landing.

integration_risks.risk: filterwarnings=error means a compatibility shim that warns fails CI.

patterns_to_follow.pattern: PEP 562 module __getattr__ with a private memoisation slot, as in notify/notify.py:89-116
Deferred import + actionable 'install async-notify[<extra>]' message, as in Telegram.py:343-347
Optional dependency with a silent ImportError guard, as in notify/utils/uv.py:14

claims.claim: notify/__init__.py imports no concrete provider; the providers package __init__ is an empty docstring.
The Notify factory already lazy-imports providers via importlib.import_module and memoises them in PROVIDERS.
claims.reasoning: direct read of LoadProvider and both factory entry points

claims.claim: No module anywhere in notify/ imports a concrete provider; all 21 provider-related imports point upward at base/mail/_mime_utils.
claims.reasoning: exhaustive grep over notify/ including the server package

claims.claim: `import notify` costs ~192ms on this machine, stable across 5 runs.
~122ms (63%) of that is navconfig and ~69ms (36%) is datamodel+jinja2; notify.providers.base has only 21ms of self time.
claims.reasoning: preload-and-remeasure attribution plus -X importtime self/cumulative split

claims.claim: base.py's datamodel edge is annotation-only (Actor) and its jinja2 edge is one pure-string predicate call (is_template_source).
claims.reasoning: every Actor reference read and confirmed to be an annotation; is_template_source body read and confirmed jinja2-free

claims.claim: A missing optional SDK surfaces as 'No Provider <x> was Found', conflating it with an unknown provider and never naming the extra.
claims.reasoning: executed probe blocking aiogram via sys.meta_path; full exception chain captured

claims.claim: LoadProvider's except-ImportError fallback re-imports the same failed classpath and, on success, returns the module rather than the provider class.
claims.reasoning: direct read; the fallback's return value differs in type from the happy path

claims.claim: pillow is declared as a core dependency but no module in notify/ imports PIL.
claims.reasoning: grep for PIL returned only unrelated activityImage field hits in models.py

claims.claim: emoji, aiobotocore and cloudpickle are core dependencies used by exactly one provider or by the server only.
claims.reasoning: grep located each to a single consumer

claims.claim: Demoting those four packages changes install weight, not `import notify` time, since none is reachable from the entrypoint.
claims.reasoning: follows from C1 and the measured import tree, which contains none of them

claims.claim: The public surface is __all__ = ('Notify','ProviderType') and tests import providers by full path, so package-level laziness is backward compatible.
claims.reasoning: direct read of __all__ plus grep over all 7 test files

claims.claim: Deferring datamodel+jinja2 out of base.py should bring `import notify` from ~192ms to ~123ms.
claims.reasoning: arithmetic from the preload attribution; not yet verified by an actual patched build, and tree overlap could shift it

claims.claim: Deferring navconfig as well could approach the ~35ms marginal floor.
claims.reasoning: the 35ms figure is the marginal cost with all three preloaded, which is a lower bound, not an achievable target; conf.py's ~20 eagerly-evaluated constants may make full deferral impractical

claims.claim: This work continues an established in-tree direction (PEP 562 TemplateEnv, optional uvloop) rather than introducing a new pattern.
claims.reasoning: two on-theme commits in the last 120 days plus two existing guard sites

claims.claim: README documents no extras at all, making the missing-SDK error unactionable even once the message is improved.
claims.reasoning: grep for install/extras keywords returned zero matches

unknowns.question: The stated premise (providers loaded eagerly regardless of installed deps) does not hold — providers are already lazy. Was the real symptom a slow `import notify`, or an error/crash when an optional SDK is missing?
plausible_answers: Slow import — startup latency is the pain
A crash/confusing error on a missing SDK
Install weight of the dependency tree
unknowns.user_answer: Error confuso sin SDK + Peso de instalación. (NO el import lento — ese es un beneficio secundario.)

unknowns.question: Is there a target for `import notify` (e.g. under 50ms), or is 'measurably faster' enough?
plausible_answers: Under 125ms — the bounded datamodel+jinja2 work suffices
No hard target, just measurable improvement
unknowns.user_answer: ~123 ms mediante los deferrals acotados (datamodel+jinja2 fuera de base.py). No se ataca navconfig en este ciclo.

unknowns.question: Is demoting emoji/aiobotocore/pillow/cloudpickle from core dependencies acceptable as a breaking install change for existing users?
plausible_answers: Yes, ship in a minor with release notes
Yes but keep them in the `default` extra
No, leave install deps alone this cycle
unknowns.user_answer: Sí, con release notes: emoji/aiobotocore/pillow/cloudpickle bajan a extras; pillow se elimina.

recommended_next_command.rationale: Los tres desconocidos están resueltos y la localización es alta-confianza y medida. El spec debe re-apuntar el feature: el objetivo primario pasa a ser el diagnóstico accionable de dependencia faltante y el adelgazamiento de las deps core; los deferrals de import quedan como beneficio secundario acotado (~192→~123 ms).
